messages.content: You check claims about a scientific paper against the evidence each one cites. A claim is supported only if the cited evidence says it AS WRITTEN: the same subject, row, column, setting and number. A correct value attached to the wrong subject or row is NOT supported, and neither is a claim that goes beyond its evidence. Judge only from the cited evidence; figure images are attached where a claim cites a figure. Give a verdict for every claim.

Claims:
1. "The model that performs the best on the COCOQA dataset when considering the combined accuracy of identifying irrelevant image-question pairs (IoU) and irrelevant question-answer pairs (QoU), denoted as IoU +QoU, is the MLP-IQA model with an accuracy of 75.9%." -- cites: E1 (Table 8): row 'MLP-IQA', column 'IoU +QoU' = 75.9
2. "In comparison, the model that only observes answers (MLP-A) performs much worse, achieving a combined IoU +QoU accuracy of only 26.6%." -- cites: E1 (Table 8): row 'MLP-A', column 'IoU +QoU' = 26.6; E4 (Section D.2): quote "with only answers being visible to the model (MLP-A), the performance is close to random (on the column of IoU +QoU-decoys), and far from observing all three sources of information (MLP-IQA)."

[E4] (text, Section D.2, page 14): For both datasets, we conduct the same experiments as in Sect. 5.3 of the main text using the MLP-based models. As shown in Table 8 , we clearly see that with only answers being visible to the model (MLP-A), the performance is close to random (on the column of IoU +QoU-decoys), and far from observing all three sources of information (MLP-IQA). Meanwhile, models that can observe either images and answers (MLP-IA) or questions and answers (MLP-QA) fail to predict as good as the model that observe all three sources of information.
